headlines.title: T Mobile (TMUS) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Cut As Analysts Split On Competition
headlines.summary: T-Mobile US is under fresh scrutiny after a modest trim to its Fair Value Estimate, which moves from US$243.38 to US$236.84 as analysts refresh their models. The shift comes alongside a split in recent commentary, with some on Wall Street treating the stock’s recent pullback and satellite headlines as an opportunity, while others see rising competition and slower growth assumptions as reasons for a more cautious stance.

headlines.title: T Mobile (TMUS) Stock May Look Reasonable On Spectrum Threat News
headlines.summary: T-Mobile US has seen its share price slide sharply in recent months, which puts a fresh spotlight on whether the current valuation really lines up with what its earnings can support. After a multi year run that is still positive over five years, the recent pullback has many holders asking if the stock now better reflects the underlying profit power of the business or if more adjustment is needed. Over the past 5 years, T-Mobile US has delivered a total return of 36.4%.

headlines.title: Why You Should Buy the Dip in T-Mobile Stock
headlines.summary: T-Mobile’s steep sell-off might offer an opportunity, as analysts see SpaceX’s threat as distant and the wireless giant’s competitive strengths remain intact.

headlines.title: How Much Could You Lose In T-Mobile Stock?
headlines.summary: T-Mobile US (TMUS) stock fell 16.7% over the past month, diverging from a 2.0% gain for the S&P 500. News reports tied a sharp drop on October 9 to a SpaceX spectrum deal, and AT&T, Verizon and Comcast each lost more than 12% over the same month. You may still think of a wireless carrier as a stock that holds up in a selloff. So how far has T-Mobile stock fallen in past market selloffs.

headlines.title: Could T-Mobile's Satellite Competition Fears Create a Buying Opportunity?
headlines.summary: T-Mobile shares hit a 52-week low after SpaceX's spectrum deal sparked satellite-disruption fears, but strong earnings, cash flow, and a Raymond James upgrade suggest the sell-off was overdone.

description: T-Mobile US, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides wireless communications services in the United States, Puerto Rico, and the United States Virgin Islands. The company offers voice, messaging, and data services to postpaid, prepaid, and wholesale and other services customers. It also provides wireless devices, including smartphones, wearables, tablets, home broadband gateways, headsets, and other mobile communication devices, as well as accessories; financing through equipment installment plans; reinsurance for device insurance policies and extended warranty contracts. The company offers services under the T-Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, and Mint Mobile brands through its owned and operated retail stores, customer care channels, national retailers, and its websites, as well as through T-Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, and Mint Mobile apps. It also sells devices to dealers and other third-party distributors for resale through independent third-party retail outlets and various third-party websites. It has 700 MHz wireless spectrum licenses. The company was founded in 1994 and is headquartered in Bellevue, Washington. T-Mobile US, Inc. operates as a subsidiary of Deutsche Telekom AG.
